records.title: Brake Pressure Accumulator ('Bomb') Nitrogen Loss
records.description: Cars using the shared engine-driven hydraulic system (power steering plus hydraulic brake assist, the 'Pentosin' system) rely on a nitrogen-charged pressure accumulator, commonly called the 'bomb,' to store hydraulic pressure for brake-assist reserve. Over roughly 7+ years the nitrogen diffuses through the internal diaphragm, so the accumulator can no longer hold a charge. The classic symptom is the brake warning light flashing briefly during firm braking, a harder/heavier brake pedal, and loss of reserve assist if the engine stalls. This is distinct from a hydraulic fluid leak, the accumulator can fail while the system is full and not leaking.
records.solution: Confirm with the standard test: engine idling, hold steering at full lock and pump the brakes hard 10-15 times; if the brake warning light comes on, suspect the bomb, pump, or drive belt. First try a fresh Pentosin (CHF) flush and clean the inline screens, as low/contaminated fluid mimics the fault. If pressure still bleeds off quickly, replace the pressure accumulator (bomb). Verify the hydraulic pump and its drive belt are healthy as part of diagnosis.
symptoms: Brake warning light flashes on hard braking
Reduced brake assist when engine stalls
Loss of stored hydraulic pressure / pedal stiffens after a few pumps

citations.title: How does the bomb (brake accumulator) work and what's the purpose? (AudiWorld)

records.title: Engine/Charging Wiring Harness Insulation Degradation
records.description: On the C4 Audi 100, the under-hood wiring insulation (notably the alternator-to-starter and engine harness sections) becomes brittle with age and heat and can literally crumble away, exposing bare conductors. This produces intermittent charging faults, hard-to-trace electrical gremlins, voltage-regulation problems, and risk of short circuits. Forum owners report the insulation 'basically disintegrated' on these harnesses. Faults are often temperature-sensitive (worse when cold, sometimes cured temporarily by a restart), making diagnosis frustrating.
records.solution: Inspect the engine and alternator/starter harness for cracked, hardened, or flaking insulation. Re-wrap or re-loom affected sections, or replace individual degraded conductors and connectors; severe cases warrant a partial harness rebuild. Check and clean battery, alternator, and ground connections. On charging complaints, also inspect the ignition switch (it supplies alternator excitation on this platform) and the voltage regulator/brushes before condemning the alternator.
symptoms: Crumbling or brittle wiring insulation under the hood
Faults worse when cold, sometimes cured by restart
Risk of short circuits / blown fuses

citations.title: quattroworld.com Forums: C4 100/A6 charging and wiring harness discussion

records.title: HVAC Temperature Flap (Blend Door) Actuator Motor Failure
records.description: The automatic climate control on the C4 Audi 100 drives the in-dash temperature and air-distribution flaps with small electric actuator motors that also report flap position back to the control head. With age the motor gearing dries out and binds, or the position feedback potentiometer goes faulty, so the climate unit cannot move a flap to the commanded position. Symptoms include heat or A/C stuck on one temperature, no/incorrect airflow to certain vents, poor defrost, and sometimes a clicking/buzzing actuator. The control head can flag a flap-motor fault when the flap can't reach its target.
records.solution: Diagnose via the climate control head's self-test to identify the affected flap motor. In many cases the actuator can be removed, cleaned of old dried grease, freed up, and re-lubricated (light oil/grease) to restore travel; a faulty feedback potentiometer or a stripped gear requires replacing the actuator. Confirm the linkage and foam flap seals are intact. Replacement is inexpensive in parts but labor-intensive due to dash access.
symptoms: Temperature stuck hot or cold regardless of setting
Clicking or buzzing from behind the dash
Climate control flags a flap-motor fault

records.title: Power Steering Rack Seal Leak
records.description: The hydraulic power steering rack develops leaks from the input shaft seal and inner tie rod boots. Pentosin hydraulic fluid weeps and eventually pours from the rack, causing heavy steering and low fluid warnings.
records.solution: Replace or rebuild power steering rack. Use Pentosin CHF 11S fluid only — conventional ATF will destroy seals. Flush entire system when replacing rack. Check pump for whining which indicates damage from running low.

records.title: Timing Belt Failure on Interference V6 Causes Catastrophic Engine Damage
records.description: The Audi 100 V6 (AAH 2.8) is an interference engine: if the timing belt breaks or jumps, valves collide with pistons, resulting in bent valves and possible head/piston damage. Owners frequently neglect this on these older, lower-value cars, and the belt, tensioner, and idlers (plus the water pump driven by the belt) age out. Because of the engine's age, rubber components and the tensioner are well past their service life on most surviving cars. A snapped belt typically writes off the engine economically.
records.solution: Replace the timing belt on the manufacturer interval (roughly every 60,000-90,000 miles, or by age on these old cars) and always replace the tensioner, idler/roller, and the water pump at the same time. Use the correct cam/crank locking tools to set timing precisely, as slight misalignment on this interference engine causes valve-to-piston contact. If a belt has already failed, a compression/leak-down test and valve inspection are required before deciding on repair vs. engine replacement.
symptoms: Engine cranks but will not start (belt snapped)
Sudden loss of power while driving
Rattle or chirp from front timing cover area

records.title: Vacuum Hose Deterioration Causing Multiple Issues
records.description: Vacuum hoses throughout the engine bay become brittle, crack, and leak with age. Causes rough idle, failed emissions, inoperative climate control flaps, and cruise control failure. The Audi 100 uses vacuum for numerous subsystems.
records.solution: Replace all vacuum hoses with silicone or OEM-quality rubber hose. Create a vacuum line diagram before removing old lines. Test each vacuum-operated system after replacement. Inspect check valves and vacuum reservoir.

citations.title: How to Diagnose and Replace Vacuum Hoses on a 1990s Audi 100 - ChrisFix
